source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Restrict routine fluids to prevent overload even when there is no clinical reason for restriction","B":"Wait until the client requests a drink because thirst remains a dependable hydration signal with age","C":"Offer fluids regularly when not contraindicated and monitor intake instead of relying only on thirst","D":"Assess hydration only once daily because frequent intake monitoring does not affect dehydration risk"}}
source_row.rationale: Older adults may not reliably increase fluid intake in response to thirst. When not contraindicated, proactive access and offering of fluids plus monitoring can help reduce dehydration risk.
source_row.source_detail: Older adults are disproportionately affected by dehydration partly because of reduced thirst sensation and dependence/access factors; current chapter accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.stem: An older adult at risk for dehydration rarely reports feeling thirsty. Which nursing intervention is most appropriate?
